user.title: Connect to UniFi
user.description: Create an API key in UniFi under Settings → Integrations, then paste it here.

site.title: Choose the site
site.description: Pick which site to police, and where approval prompts should go. Sites are listed alphabetically.

error.cannot_connect: Could not reach the controller. Check the URL and port.
error.invalid_auth: The controller rejected that API key.

abort.already_configured: That site is already set up.

data.enforced_ssids: Only police these SSIDs (leave empty for all)
data.max_per_run: Stop and alert if more than this appear at once
data.min_list_guard: Minimum allow list size before blocking
data.deny_unnamed: Always block devices that report no name
data.forget_in_unifi: Also remove the client from UniFi when forgetting

data_description.adopt_blocks: Each poll, move devices blocked in the UniFi UI into Denied, and re-apply blocks that were removed there. Off by default.
data_description.deny_names: One entry per name, case insensitive, * and ? wildcards allowed. A plain word also matches anywhere in the name. Matching devices are blocked silently with no notification and no queue entry. Where the panel shows a name with the MAC appended, such as 'Tesla a2:fb', either form works - the plain name catches every client using it, the suffixed one catches only that device. Names come from the device and can be changed, so treat this as noise control rather than security.
data_description.deny_unnamed: Devices with no hostname at all. This catches a lot of legitimate hardware such as cameras and IoT gear, so check the waiting list before turning it on.
data_description.forget_in_unifi: Deletes the client record on the controller, the same as Forget in the UniFi UI - alias, fixed IP and history included, with no undo. Clients that have a name or a fixed IP set in UniFi are only unblocked instead, so nothing you configured there is destroyed.
data_description.min_list_guard: An optional hard floor: below this many allowed devices, nothing is blocked at all. Off by default, because losing the stored list is caught separately and a fixed number suits a large site far better than a small one. Set it only if you want a belt-and-braces floor of your own.
data_description.sms_numbers: Needs the Telebroad SMS integration. Each waiting device is texted with a short id; reply '475 allow' or '475 keep'. Only these numbers are acted on, and only for this site.
data_description.sms_line: Leave blank to use the first configured Telebroad line.
data_description.sms_pin: Caller ID can be faked, so anyone who learns the line number and the id format could reply. With a PIN set, replies must read '475 allow 4321'. Blank means no PIN.
data_description.sms_digest: One text listing several devices instead of one text each. Useful on a busy night; off means every device gets its own message.
data_description.scan_interval: How often the connected-device list is read. This is the small, cheap call, so lowering it shortens the window an unknown device has before it is blocked without much extra load. The full client list refreshes once a minute regardless. Going below about 15s risks a busy run overlapping the next poll; lower the pause between alerts too if you do.
